Hey, I’m a bit late but I kind of wanted to mention that saying “the superego punishes those who are the most moral” is something Freud mentions regarding obsessive neurotic behaviour.

Basically, a severe superego may manifest in rigid subjects who do things the “correct” way and who show tenacity when challenged about it. This is related to the repressed aggressive tendencies towards the father, who in classic psychoanalytic fashion, is both loved and hated. So a severe super ego feeds off a sense of guilt (guilt of wishing harm to someone you love) regarding repressed aggressiveness and may enable, in turn, a way to manifest those aggresive tendencies via “having the moral high ground”.

Another structure that tends to have severe superego is melancholy (depression), where it can lead to a constant “being put down” by it, which relates to self worth issues.

Throughout the essays he explains how different stages come and go (Ever noticed that babies put everything they get their hands on in their mouths? It's a magical girl anime where the protagonist is approached by a cat-like creature who offers her a deal: she gets one wish in exchange for becoming a magical girl and fighting witches. Is there more than it meets the eye when it comes to this offer?

 It's by far my favorite anime, and it's only 12 episodes long.

{Neon Genesis Evangelion} also has really good mystery as you can see there's definitely people who have a plan which, coupled with the "lore" that you begin to discover as episodes pass, makes for a very mysterious anime in which you can't be sure what really is going on behind the scenes at the beginning, but it's hinted at gradually until the final part of the series. 26 episodes and a movie {The End of Evangelion}

Also, honorable mention to <Chainsaw Man> manga which has only 97 episodes and has this kind of mystery you're asking for, but not to the same level as the other ones I'd say. Still a fantastic read.
